topStories.headline: Marina Safeway Tower Clears August Design Deadline — With a Shorter Profile and More Units
topStories.dek: Developer Align Real Estate revised its controversial mixed-use tower at 15 Marina Blvd., trimming height while adding apartments, as the state-mandated design-review clock expired.
topStories.body:
The long-running battle over the Marina Safeway site reached a pivotal moment this week as the San Francisco Planning Department's state-mandated design-review deadline passed. Developer Align Real Estate, filing on behalf of property owner Albertsons Companies, submitted updated plans in mid-July that reduced the project's tallest towers from 25 and 22 stories to 22 and 18 stories, while simultaneously increasing the residential unit count from 790 to 848 apartments. The redesign trims roughly 40 feet from the east tower and 23 feet from the west tower, with the full development at 15 Marina Boulevard spanning approximately 989,500 square feet.

The revisions came after months of fierce community opposition. Residents staged protests outside the existing Safeway store beginning in April, arguing that the development would reshape the neighborhood's skyline and that the project's handful of below-market-rate units — 86 out of 848 — did not meaningfully address affordability. The SF Standard, in a piece published August 2, framed the outcome bluntly: state housing laws passed over the last decade have stripped cities of much of their traditional discretionary review authority when developers meet certain affordability thresholds under Assembly Bill 2011.

The project — designed by Miami-based firm Arquitectonica — would replace the 1959 Wurster-designed single-story Safeway with two residential towers rising from a shared podium, plus a 67,180-square-foot replacement grocery store and a 349-car garage. The development would be the tallest structure on San Francisco's northern waterfront.

District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, who represents the Marina, has publicly opposed the design, and opponents mounted a late legal challenge in June arguing that the site may not qualify for AB 2011 fast-tracking because the surrounding area does not meet the law's threshold for existing urban development. If city officials ultimately agree, Align could be forced back into a full environmental review, adding years to the timeline.

topStories.headline: Monami Korean BBQ Begins Construction on Upper Fillmore, Targeting Fall Opening
topStories.dek: The Michelin-starred founders of SSAL on Polk Street are renovating the long-vacant Noosh space at 2001 Fillmore to open an upscale Korean barbecue restaurant this fall.
topStories.body:
Construction is now underway at 2001 Fillmore Street in Pacific Heights, where Junsoo and Hyunyoung Bae — the founders of Michelin-starred SSAL on upper Polk Street — are building Monami, a new upscale Korean barbecue restaurant. Upstairs tenants at the building received notice in April that they needed to vacate to make way for ground-floor construction, which began June 1. An opening is targeted for fall 2026.

Chef Junsoo Bae has described his vision for the restaurant as a Korean barbecue analog to House of Prime Rib — a theatrical, destination-dining experience rather than a casual grill. The space at 2001 Fillmore, which has housed a rotating roster of restaurants for decades including Pacific Heights Bar & Grill, Thai Stick, and the well-regarded Noosh, has sat vacant for nearly two years.

The arrival of Monami is part of a broader effort to revitalize Upper Fillmore. The restaurant is understood to have received support from the Upper Fillmore Revitalization Project, an initiative that has also invested in the neighboring Clay Theatre. The project signals continued confidence in the Fillmore corridor as a dining destination, though the block-level disruption of construction has drawn attention from residents and nearby businesses.

topStories.headline: Supervisor Sherrill Wins District 2 Special Election by Wide Margin, November Race Ahead
topStories.dek: Incumbent Stephen Sherrill captured roughly 70 percent of the vote in the June 2 special election, keeping his seat through the end of the year and setting up a full-term contest in November.
topStories.body:
District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill decisively won the June 2, 2026 special election to retain his seat on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, defeating challenger Lori Brooke 70 percent to 30 percent in early results. Sherrill, a moderate ally of Mayor Daniel Lurie, was originally appointed to the seat in December 2024 by then-Mayor London Breed after Supervisor Catherine Stefani was elected to the California State Assembly.

Sherrill's district covers the Marina, Cow Hollow, Pacific Heights, and Presidio Heights — some of the city's most affluent and closely watched neighborhoods. His campaign emphasized public safety, reducing bureaucratic red tape for small businesses, and working collaboratively with Mayor Lurie's administration. Brooke, a neighborhood activist and organizer, had hoped to leverage local anger over the Marina Safeway redevelopment project and Sherrill's support for the mayor's Family Zoning plan, which allowed denser residential development in parts of the city.

Sherrill will hold the seat through the end of the year. The November 3, 2026 general election will determine who represents District 2 for a full four-year term. His strong showing in the special election means he enters that race as the clear frontrunner, though other candidates may still enter the field.

moreNews.headline: New Cow Hollow Infill Would Add 15 Units at 2629 Lombard Street
moreNews.body: Plans filed in mid-July call for a six-story residential building at 2629 Lombard Street in Cow Hollow, replacing a two-story house a couple of blocks from the Presidio. The proposal, designed by Studio 12 Architecture and invoking the Housing Choice San Francisco program, would yield approximately 20,550 square feet across 15 units — two studios, seven one-bedrooms, and six two-bedrooms — with no on-site parking. The filing is the latest in a wave of mid-scale infill applications reshaping Lombard Street's residential corridor.

moreNews.headline: Cow Hollow Real Estate Hits Record Overbid Territory in 2026
moreNews.body: Cow Hollow's housing market continued its torrid pace through mid-2026, with condo buyers paying an average of 118.3 percent of list price in April, according to Compass market data cited by Helena 7x7. The 12-month rolling median house price in the neighborhood reached $6,450,000, with individual sales as high as $16.8 million. The SF Standard reported in May that a lack of inventory — just 835 single-family homes listed citywide as of April 1, versus a typical 1,100 — has collided with a deep roster of buyers, pushing overbids to near-record levels across the Marina cluster.

moreNews.headline: Upper Fillmore Revitalization Gains Momentum with New Tenants and Theater Reactivation
moreNews.body: The Upper Fillmore corridor in Pacific Heights is showing signs of a commercial revival in summer 2026. In addition to the forthcoming Monami Korean barbecue restaurant at 2001 Fillmore, a real estate market analysis by Ray Amouzandeh documented new restaurant openings, a newly operational Clay Theatre, and a returning retailer along the stretch between Sacramento and Pine streets. The activity builds on an organized revitalization effort that has drawn support from District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill and Mayor Daniel Lurie's administration.
moreNews.sourceName: Ray Realtor / Upper Fillmore Revitalization Project

restaurants.name: Wilder

restaurants.name: The Tipsy Pig
restaurants.description: Distinctly Californian Marina gastropub serving locally sourced craft cocktails and comfort food since 2009, a neighborhood anchor on Chestnut Street.

restaurants.name: Perry's

restaurants.name: Pizzeria Delfina

restaurants.name: Palm House

hotels.name: Hotel Del Sol

hotels.name: Cow Hollow Inn & Suites
hotels.description: Well-located Cow Hollow inn offering spacious suites with a loyal repeat-guest following, situated between Lombard and Union Streets near top restaurants and shops.

hotels.name: Pacific Heights Inn
hotels.description: A comfortable, well-priced inn positioned between Cow Hollow and the Marina with the rare amenity of free on-site parking and easy access to Highway 101.

hotels.name: Greenwich Inn

shops.description: San Francisco–born shoe brand's Fillmore Street flagship, selling its signature machine-washable flats, sneakers, and bags made from recycled plastic bottles.

shops.name: Isalis

shops.name: Sézane
shops.description: San Francisco outpost of the beloved Parisian brand offering women's and men's clothing with a signature relaxed-chic aesthetic on Pacific Heights' Fillmore corridor.

shops.name: Cuyana
shops.description: SF-founded brand known for its 'fewer, better things' philosophy, offering elevated essentials in leather goods, clothing, and accessories at its Pacific Heights shop.

shops.description: Refined Pacific Heights shop dedicated to single-origin teas from China and Taiwan, paired with a curated collection of handcrafted ceramics for the serious tea drinker.

shops.name: Sloat Garden Center (Marina)

artEntertainment.name: Palace of Fine Arts Theatre

artEntertainment.name: Haas-Lilienthal House
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's only intact grand Victorian private home open regularly as a museum, offering docent-led tours of the exuberant 1886 Queen Anne structure that survived the 1906 earthquake.

gymsRecreation.description: Dedicated Iyengar yoga studio near Pacific Heights offering in-studio and online classes for all levels, plus advanced studies workshops and teacher training.
